Rim-mass pulley coupled to a hanging mass ((M+m)Rθ¨+Mgsinθ−mg=0)

Words: 62
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
A massless fixed-axis pulley carries a rim point mass M at radius R. A mechanical string gripping its rim without slipping passes over a fixed guide pulley to a hanging mass m. Choose the angle θ from downward vertical so the hanging mass descends by Rθ. The Lagrangian is (M+m)R2θ˙2/2+MgRcosθ+mgRθ. The stable equilibrium satisfies sinθe​=m/M with cosθe​>0, and exists for 0<m<M. Its small-amplitude angular frequency is [Mgcosθe​/((M+m)R)]1/2.

Chain sliding over a table edge ((M+m+ρL)x¨=g(M+ρx))

Words: 149 Articles: 1
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
An inextensible uniform chain of length L and linear mass density ρ links a mass m sliding on a frictionless table to a hanging mass M. If the initial hanging chain length is zero and x is its subsequent hanging length, all moving material has speed x˙. The kinetic energy is (M+m+ρL)x˙2/2, while the gravitational potential energy is −Mgx−ρgx2/2. The Euler-Lagrange equation gives the displayed equation until a mass hits the floor or reaches the edge. Increasing hanging chain weight produces a hyperbolic cosine displacement from rest, rather than uniform acceleration.

Spring-stabilized chain over a table edge (ω2=(k−ρg)/(M+m+ρL))

Words: 65
Chain sliding over a table edge OurBigBook.com
Attach the table-end mass to a linear spring of spring constant k. Adding spring potential energy k(e0​+x)2/2 gives restoring curvature k−ρg about equilibrium. The positive gravitational feedback from increasing hanging chain length subtracts from the spring stiffness. Stable oscillations require k>ρg; equality is neutral in this ideal linear model, while k<ρg gives exponential departure. The frequency is independent of the preload, although the equilibrium position is not.

Routhian mechanics

Words: 111 Articles: 1
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
A reduction of Lagrangian mechanics that fixes conserved momenta of cyclic coordinates while keeping an Euler-Lagrange description for the remaining coordinates. It is named for Edward Routh. The Routhian applies a partial Legendre transform to the eliminated velocities.

Routhian (R=L−∑i​pi​q˙​i​)

Words: 81
Routhian mechanics OurBigBook.com
Use the convention R=L−∑i​pi​q˙​i​ for the eliminated cyclic coordinates, expressing their velocities in terms of their fixed conjugate momenta. Terms involving derivatives of those eliminated velocities cancel because ∂L/∂q˙​i​=pi​. Thus the remaining coordinates obey the usual Euler-Lagrange equations for R. For a particle of fixed angular momentum ℓ in a central potential, this gives R=mr˙2/2−V(r)−ℓ2/(2mr2), rather than the expression obtained by direct substitution into L alone. An opposite overall sign convention is also used, with correspondingly signed mixed Hamiltonian equations.

Lagrangian energy function (E=∑i​q˙​i​∂L/∂q˙​i​−L)

Words: 54
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
For a Lagrangian L(q,q˙​,t), its energy function satisfies dE/dt=−∂L/∂t along the Euler-Lagrange equations. This follows by differentiating and cancelling the q¨​i​∂L/∂q˙​i​ terms. It is conserved when L has no explicit time dependence. For imposed moving constraints it need not coincide with inertial mechanical energy; a Jacobi integral is an important example.

Frictionless sliding ladder

Words: 85
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
For a uniform slender ladder of length 2l sliding while touching a smooth wall and floor, use its angle θ from the vertical. Its centre of mass is (lsinθ,lcosθ) and its central moment of inertia is ml2/3. Hence the Lagrangian is L=2ml2θ˙2/3−mglcosθ, and its Euler-Lagrange equation is θ¨=3gsinθ/(4l). The contacts are physically possible only while their normal forces are nonnegative. If released from rest at θ0​, energy conservation gives θ˙2=3g(cosθ0​−cosθ)/(2l), and the wall force becomes 3mgsinθ(3cosθ−2cosθ0​)/4. Contact is lost at cosθ=2cosθ0​/3, after which the constrained equation no longer describes the motion.

Elastic pendulum (L=21​m(r˙2+r2θ˙2)−21​k(r−l)2+mgrcosθ)

Words: 65
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
A point mass attached to a massless straight spring can change its radial distance r from a fixed support while swinging in a vertical plane. Its lower equilibrium length is r0​=l+mg/k. Linearizing the Euler-Lagrange equations there gives independent radial and angular normal modes with squared angular frequencies k/m and g/r0​. The formal upper stationary state has r=l−mg/k and exists in positive-length coordinates only when l>mg/k; its angular mode is unstable.

Tabletop mass coupled to a hanging mass (UJ​(r)=J2/(2mr2)+Mgr−Mgl)

Words: 63
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
A tabletop mass m joined through a hole by a massless inextensible string of length l to a hanging mass M has radial inertia M+m and conserved angular momentum J=mr2θ˙. The radial energy is 21​(M+m)r˙2+UJ​(r), with 0<r<l. Its effective potential diverges at the hole for J=0 and has a unique minimum at r03​=J2/(mMg). Since UJ′′​(r0​)=3Mg/r0​, small radial oscillations at fixed J have squared angular frequency 3Mg/[(M+m)r0​].

Atwood machine

Words: 250 Articles: 2
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
An Atwood machine couples two hanging masses by an inextensible mechanical string over a pulley. With ideal massless hardware, Newton's second law gives the downward acceleration of the heavier mass as a=g(m2​−m1​)/(m1​+m2​). To prove it, write m2​g−T=m2​a and T−m1​g=m1​a, then add. The apparatus associated with George Atwood turns a small difference of weights into slow, measurable acceleration.

Leaking Atwood machine (vempty​=αgM0​​[−ϵ−2log(1−ϵ/2)])

Words: 123
Atwood machine OurBigBook.com
Two initially equal buckets of total mass M0​ share an ideal Atwood machine. If one loses sand at constant rate α and the sand leaves with zero initial velocity relative to that bucket, the leakage supplies no rocket thrust. The remaining masses satisfy (M+M0​)v˙=g(M0​−M) for upward velocity of the leaking side. Using M˙=−α and integrating from rest gives v=(g/α)[M−M0​−2M0​log((M+M0​)/(2M0​))].
If the initial sand fraction is ϵ, emptying occurs at M=(1−ϵ)M0​. This gives the displayed speed, which tends to zero for ϵ→0 and to (gM0​/α)(2log2−1) for ϵ→1−. The latter is a finite limiting result, not a physical claim about an exactly massless empty bucket. The derivation is an application of a variable-mass system, rather than of d(Mv)/dt=F for a closed body.

Compound Atwood machine

Words: 80
Atwood machine OurBigBook.com
A compound Atwood machine replaces one hanging mass by another pulley carrying two masses. Let the upper mechanical string carry mass M opposite the moving pulley, and let the lower mechanical string carry masses a,b at upward heights x,y. The length constraints on the mechanical strings give the height of M as −(x+y)/2 up to a constant. Thus its Lagrangian is
L=8M​(x˙+y˙​)2+2a​x˙2+2b​y˙​2−g[(a−2M​)x+(b−2M​)y].
(1)
This follows by adding the three kinetic energies and subtracting their gravitational potential energies. Constant coordinate shifts annihilating the linear potential energy give conserved generalized momentum components by Noether's theorem.

Jacobi integral (J=E−ωLz​)

Words: 88
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
For a mechanical system whose imposed motion is uniform rotation with angular velocity ω about a fixed axis, a conserved rotating-frame energy can exist even when the inertial mechanical energy E changes. With angular momentum Lz​ about that axis, it is J=E−ωLz​. For a bead constrained to rotate with θ˙=ω, this becomes
J=2m​(r˙2+z˙2)+V−2m​ω2r2.
(2)
For z=r2/(2a) in uniform gravity, division by mass yields
mJ​=21​(1+a2r2​)r˙2+21​(ag​−ω2)r2.
(3)
This is the first integral that controls the bead's radial motion. Different normalizations and signs are used for the related Jacobi constant in celestial mechanics.

Pendulum with a freely sliding support (Meff​(ϕ)=m2​l2(m1​+m2​sin2ϕ)/(m1​+m2​))

Words: 90 Articles: 1
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
For a pendulum whose support slides without horizontal force, the support coordinate is cyclic and total horizontal momentum is conserved. At zero horizontal momentum, eliminating support velocity leaves the displayed angle-dependent effective inertia. The energy is Meff​ϕ˙​2/2−m2​glcosϕ. Fixing the momentum before evaluating motion is distinct from fixing the support position.

Elliptic bob path at zero horizontal momentum ((X−Xc​)2/[lm1​/(m1​+m2​)]2+Y2/l2=1)

Words: 42
Pendulum with a freely sliding support OurBigBook.com
Zero horizontal momentum fixes the horizontal centre of mass. The bob coordinates become X=Xc​+lm1​sinϕ/(m1​+m2​) and Y=−lcosϕ. Eliminating the angle gives an ellipse; an ordinary oscillation traverses only its permitted arc. The support counter-moves, so the bob's path differs from the circle about a fixed pivot.

Degenerate Lagrangian

Words: 58
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
A Lagrangian is degenerate when its Hessian with respect to velocities is singular. The momentum–velocity relation then cannot be inverted for every velocity. Some Euler–Lagrange equations can become algebraic constraints rather than independent second-order equations. A massless limit can produce this behaviour; disappearance of an equation at quadratic order does not establish an unconstrained mode of the exact nonlinear model.

Charged circular elastic ring in a uniform magnetic field (J=mr2ϕ˙​+qBr2/2)

Words: 190 Articles: 3
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
A uniformly charged circular ring has
L=2m​(r˙2+r2ϕ˙​2)−2π2k(r−r0​)2+2qBr2​ϕ˙​.
(4)
Here k is the spring constant for extension of its full circumference and the symmetric gauge is used. The canonical angular momentum J=mr2ϕ˙​+qBr2/2 is conserved. Eliminating the angle gives mr¨=J2/(mr3)−q2B2r/(4m)−4π2k(r−r0​). This model neglects electric self-interaction and noncircular deformation.

Turning radius of an initially stationary magnetic ring

Words: 62
Charged circular elastic ring in a uniform magnetic field OurBigBook.com
For negligible natural radius and release from rest at r1​, J=qBr12​/2. The effective radial potential is a sum of r−2 and r2 terms, whose two turning radii have squared product J2/(m2Ω2). Hence
rmin​=q2B2+16π2km​∣qB∣r1​​,ϕ˙​min​=qB8π2k​,r˙min​=0.
(5)
These formulas assume qB=0. At exactly zero field the ideal ring collapses to zero radius instead of making a regular positive-radius turning point.

Zero-canonical-angular-momentum ring oscillation (Ω2=4π2k/m+q2B2/(4m2))

Words: 55
Charged circular elastic ring in a uniform magnetic field OurBigBook.com
With J=0, define ωs2​=4π2k/m and ωc​=qB/m. Then re​=ωs2​r0​/(ωs2​+ωc2​/4), the radial frequency is Ω=ωs2​+ωc2​/4​, and release at r0​ gives r=re​+(r0​−re​)cosΩt with ϕ˙​=−ωc​/2. The physical solution requires r>0. If 2re​<r0​, the formal oscillation reaches zero and cannot be continued as a negative ring radius without a new collapse model.

Canonical Hamiltonian of a magnetic elastic ring

Words: 30
Charged circular elastic ring in a uniform magnetic field OurBigBook.com
Although the energy in velocities is m(r˙2+r2ϕ˙​2)/2+2π2k(r−r0​)2, the Hamiltonian in canonical variables is
H=2mpr2​​+2mr2(pϕ​−qBr2/2)2​+2π2k(r−r0​)2.
(6)
The field therefore enters Hamilton's equations through the relation between canonical and mechanical momentum, even though a magnetic field does no work.

Moving mechanical constraint

Words: 37
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
A constraint that depends explicitly on time can exert a normal force that does actual work, even when its force does no work on an allowed instantaneous virtual displacement. The surface motion gives the constrained particle a normal component of actual velocity.

Hoop with a suspended counterweight ((M+m)Rθ¨=g(m−Msinθ))

Words: 97
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
A point mass M attached to a massless rotating hoop of radius R is connected by a taut string wrapping around the hoop to a vertically suspended mass m. Measure θ from the downward radius toward the string's tangency side. The wrapped length decreases by Rθ, so the suspended mass descends by the same amount. Therefore T=(M+m)R2θ˙2/2 and V=−MgRcosθ−mgRθ up to a constant. The Euler-Lagrange equation gives the displayed equation. For 0<m<M, the stable equilibrium has sinθ0​=m/M, and the small-oscillation angular frequency is ω=g/R​[(M−m)/(M+m)]1/4. When M≫m, the system approaches a simple pendulum of length R.

Generalized coordinate (qi​)

Words: 84 Articles: 1
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
A generalized coordinate is one of a set of independent parameters specifying the configuration of a mechanical system subject to its constraints. An angle locates a bead constrained to a fixed circular hoop. Expressing kinetic energy and potential energy in these coordinates gives the Lagrangian and its Euler-Lagrange equations.

Generalized velocity (q˙​i​=dqi​/dt)

Words: 43
Generalized coordinate OurBigBook.com
The time derivative of a generalized coordinate. It is an independent velocity argument of a mechanical Lagrangian, but need not have the units or direction of a Cartesian velocity: for an angular coordinate it is an angular velocity. A regular Legendre transform replaces these variables with the corresponding canonical momenta.

Cartan form of a regular mechanical Lagrangian (θL​=Lvi​dqi,ωL​=−dθL​)

Words: 57
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
A regular Lagrangian L:TQ→R defines a fibre derivative FL:TQ→T∗Q and the Cartan one-form θL​=(FL)∗θ. Its two-form ωL​=−dθL​ is nondegenerate when the velocity Hessian is invertible. The energy is EL​=viLvi​−L. The equation ιΓL​​ωL​=dEL​ determines the Euler–Lagrange vector field. A hyperregular Lagrangian makes the fibre derivative a global diffeomorphism and transports this dynamics to Hamiltonian phase space.

Helical symmetry of a potential

Words: 22
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
A potential V(r,ϕ,z)=f(r,ϕ−kz) is invariant under the screw transformation (ϕ,z)↦(ϕ+ks,z+s). The Noether conserved quantity for a mechanical point symmetry is
pz​+kpϕ​,
(7)
a linear combination of axial linear momentum and axial angular momentum.

Cyclic coordinate

Words: 15
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
A generalized coordinate absent from the Lagrangian is cyclic. Its conjugate generalized momentum is conserved by the Euler-Lagrange equations.

Action (S)

Words: 42 Articles: 1
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
The action of a path is the time integral of its Lagrangian. The principle of stationary action requires its first variation to vanish for every admissible fixed-endpoint variation.

Principle of stationary action

Words: 18
Action OurBigBook.com
The principle of stationary action says that the physical path between fixed endpoints is a stationary point of the action.

Total-time-derivative invariance of a Lagrangian

Words: 25
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
Replacing a Lagrangian by
L′(q,q˙​,t)=L(q,q˙​,t)+dtd​F(q,t)
(8)
adds only the endpoint term F(q(t2​),t2​)−F(q(t1​),t1​) to the action. Fixed-endpoint variations therefore give the same Euler--Lagrange equations.

Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
For electromagnetic scalar and vector potentials ϕ and A,
L=21​mr˙2−qϕ+qr˙⋅A.
(9)
With
E=−∇ϕ−∂t​A,B=∇×A,
(10)
the Euler--Lagrange equations give the Lorentz force mr¨=q(E+r˙×B), while the canonical momentum is p=mr˙+qA.

Charged-particle electromagnetic Lagrangian OurBigBook.com
The Legendre transform of the charged-particle electromagnetic Lagrangian is
H(x,p,t)=2m[p−qA(x,t)]2​+qϕ(x,t).
(11)

Gauge variation of the charged-particle Lagrangian

Words: 28
Charged-particle electromagnetic Lagrangian OurBigBook.com
Under ϕ↦ϕ−∂t​f and A↦A+∇f, the charged-particle Lagrangian changes by
L′−L=q(∂t​f+r˙⋅∇f)=qdtdf(r(t),t)​.
(12)
It therefore has unchanged equations of motion by total-time-derivative invariance.

Canonical momentum parallel to a uniform magnetic field

Words: 43
Charged-particle electromagnetic Lagrangian OurBigBook.com
For a constant uniform magnetic field B, choose the symmetric gauge A=21​B×r. The coordinate parallel to B is cyclic, so its canonical momentum is conserved. Since A⋅B=0, this component is also the mechanical momentum mr˙⋅B.

Generalized momentum

Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
The generalized, or conjugate, momentum associated with a coordinate qi​ is
pi​=∂q˙​i​∂L​.
(13)
In Lagrangian mechanics, the coordinate variable describes the configuration; its conjugate momentum need not equal the Cartesian mechanical momentum.

Ignorable coordinate

Words: 26
Generalized momentum OurBigBook.com
A coordinate qi​ is ignorable, or cyclic, when ∂L/∂qi​=0. The Euler--Lagrange equation then gives p˙​i​=0, so its generalized momentum is conserved.

If a Lagrangian is independent of a coordinate, the conjugate momentum to that coordinate is conserved by the Euler--Lagrange equations.

Axially symmetric isotropic-mass Lagrangian

Words: 48
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
If L=∣q˙​∣2/2−V(q) and V depends only on ∣q∣2 and (q⋅n)2, then rotations about the axis n leave L invariant. The quantity supplied by Noether theorem is the axial angular momentum
Jn​=n⋅(q×q˙​).
(14)
If L also has no explicit time dependence, the energy ∣q˙​∣2/2+V(q) is conserved independently.

Double pendulum

Words: 889 Articles: 4
Lagrangian mechanics OurBigBook.com
A double pendulum consists of two pendula coupled because the second pivot moves with the first mass. It has two degrees of freedom: even when the upper pivot is fixed, moving the upper arm carries the lower pivot along. This makes the double pendulum a compact example of how mechanical constraints couple motion, and how Lagrangian mechanics converts geometry into dynamics.
Use two equal point masses m>0 and two massless rigid rods of equal length ℓ>0, with joints that allow free rotation in one vertical plane. The upper pivot is fixed; gravity is uniform, with gravitational acceleration g>0. Neglect joint friction and drag force. Both angles θ1​,θ2​ are measured from the downward vertical, positive toward the right, in radians. In particular, θ2​ is an absolute angle, not the bend between the rods: that bend is θ2​−θ1​.
The double pendulum Lagrangian below gives the exact dynamics of this ideal model. Near the downward stable equilibrium, normal modes of a double pendulum replace the coupled motion with two independent harmonic oscillators. Their fixed amplitude ratios explain which releases make the rods swing together and which make them swing in opposite directions.

Double pendulum with an end-to-end spring

Words: 43
Double pendulum OurBigBook.com
With equal rod lengths ℓ and absolute downward-vertical angles θ,ϕ, the endpoint separation is s2=2ℓ2[1+cos(θ−ϕ)]. A zero-rest-length spring between the fixed support and the final mass contributes −κℓ2[1+cos(θ−ϕ)] to the Lagrangian. It favours bending away from maximum extension and can reduce the gravitational bending stiffness.

Double pendulum Lagrangian (L=T−V)

Words: 227
Double pendulum OurBigBook.com
Choose Cartesian coordinates with origin at the upper pivot, x to the right and y upward. The two position vectors are
r1​=ℓ(sinθ1​−cosθ1​​),r2​=ℓ(sinθ1​+sinθ2​−cosθ1​−cosθ2​​).
(15)
These expressions satisfy the rod holonomic constraints ∣r1​∣=ℓ and ∣r2​−r1​∣=ℓ automatically. This is the practical advantage of using the two angles as coordinates: the rod tensions need not be unknowns in the motion calculation.[ref]
Differentiate these position vectors to obtain the velocities. The dot product between their two rod contributions uses cos(θ1​−θ2​)=cosθ1​cosθ2​+sinθ1​sinθ2​, giving
∣r˙1​∣2=ℓ2θ˙12​,∣r˙2​∣2=ℓ2(θ˙12​+θ˙22​+2cos(θ1​−θ2​)θ˙1​θ˙2​).
(16)
Adding the two kinetic energies and measuring gravitational potential energy from the downward equilibrium gives
TVL​=2mℓ2​(2θ˙12​+θ˙22​+2cos(θ1​−θ2​)θ˙1​θ˙2​),=mgℓ[2(1−cosθ1​)+(1−cosθ2​)],=T−V.​
(17)
The coefficient 2 has a geometric meaning: the upper rod raises both masses, and its motion contributes to both kinetic energies. The coupling in T is present because the lower mass has a moving pivot. The zero chosen for V changes L by a constant and leaves the Euler-Lagrange equations unchanged.[ref]
The principle of stationary action applies to S=∫Ldt. Its fixed-endpoint first variation, after integration by parts, is
δS=∫∑i=12​(∂θi​∂L​−dtd​∂θ˙i​∂L​)δθi​dt.
(18)
Independent allowed variations therefore give one Euler-Lagrange equation for each angle. Stationary action alone does not assert a minimum.[ref]

Double pendulum equations of motion

Words: 209
Double pendulum OurBigBook.com
Write Δ=θ1​−θ2​. Applying the Euler-Lagrange equations to the double pendulum Lagrangian, then dividing by mℓ2, gives
2θ¨1​+cosΔθ¨2​+sinΔθ˙22​+ℓ2g​sinθ1​cosΔθ¨1​+θ¨2​−sinΔθ˙12​+ℓg​sinθ2​​=0,=0.​
(19)
For example, the upper generalized momentum is ∂L/∂θ˙1​=mℓ2(2θ˙1​+cosΔθ˙2​). Its time derivative contains −mℓ2sinΔ(θ˙1​−θ˙2​)θ˙2​. Subtracting ∂L/∂θ1​=−mℓ2sinΔθ˙1​θ˙2​−2mgℓsinθ1​ cancels the mixed product and leaves the positive sinΔθ˙22​ term in the first equation. This cancellation is a useful check on the sign convention.
The matrix multiplying the two angular accelerations is
(2cosΔ​cosΔ1​),det=2−cos2Δ≥1.
(20)
It is invertible for every configuration, so specified angles and angular velocities determine both angular accelerations. For the same reason T>0 whenever the angular velocities are not both zero. The mass cancels from the motion equations, while the timescale is set by ℓ/g​.
As an exact constructed release, put θ1​(0)=α, θ2​(0)=0, and both angular velocities zero. Solving the two equations at release yields
θ¨1​(0)=−ℓ2g​2−cos2αsinα​,θ¨2​(0)=ℓ2g​2−cos2αsinαcosα​.

Its potential energy is k∑i<j​(Xi​−Xj​)2/2. The moving-coordinate stiffness matrix is the principal submatrix displayed in the header. For equal masses m, the uniform normal mode has squared angular frequency k/m, while every sum-zero vector has squared angular frequency (n+1)k/m. There are n−1 such degenerate modes. This follows directly from the Laplacian spectrum of a complete graph and its rank-one matrix form. Constant gravitational forces shift the equilibrium without changing the stiffness.
Octave tuning in a two-mass complete spring graph (m2​/m1​=(43±533​)/32)
Words: 84
Normal modes of an anchored complete spring graph OurBigBook.com
For two masses, connect each to a fixed anchor and to the other mass with equal stiffness k. Set m1​=1,k=1 to choose units. The squared angular frequencies have characteristic equation m2​z2−2(m2​+1)z+3=0. Requiring a frequency ratio of two means that these roots are z and 4z. Their sum and product give 16m22​−43m2​+16=0, yielding the two reciprocal ratios in the header. Restoring units multiplies all squared frequencies by k/m1​, leaving the permitted mass ratios unchanged. The term octave refers here only to this two-to-one ratio.
Normal modes of three equal masses with a symmetric gap potential
Words: 51
Degenerate normal modes from permutation symmetry OurBigBook.com
Let three equal masses move on a circle of radius r, and let the potential be U(α)+U(β)+U(γ) with α+β+γ=2π. At equal spacing s0​=2π/3, angular displacements have a zero-frequency rigid-rotation mode (1,1,1) and a two-dimensional sum-zero eigenspace with
ω2=mr23U′′(s0​)​.
(44)
The two vibrational modes are degenerate by the permutation symmetry.

Words: 47
Degenerate normal modes from permutation symmetry OurBigBook.com
For three unit masses with unit springs between every pair and one unit spring anchoring each mass to the origin,
M=I,K=4I−J,
(45)
where J is the all-ones matrix. The collective mode (1,1,1) has angular frequency 1, while the two-dimensional sum-zero subspace has angular frequency 2.

Normal modes of two equal masses between three springs

Words: 128 Articles: 1
Generalized eigenvalue problem for small oscillations OurBigBook.com
For equal masses m, wall-spring constants k1​,k2​, and coupling-spring constant k3​, the small-oscillation mass and stiffness matrices are
M=mI,K=(k1​+k3​−k3​​−k3​k2​+k3​​).
(46)
If k1​=k(1+εδ), k2​=k(1−εδ), and k3​=kε, the squared normal frequencies are
ω±2​=mk​[1+ε(1±1+δ2​)].
(47)
First turning point of an initially stationary coupled oscillator (tanz∗​=−z∗​)
Words: 88
Normal modes of two equal masses between three springs OurBigBook.com
For two equal masses with equal wall springs released with displacements (d,0), their second displacement is x2​=dsin(ωˉt)sin(δt), where ωˉ is the mean of the two positive normal mode frequencies and 2δ their difference. The first nonzero time with x˙2​=0 is a fast turning point, not the slow maximum of its beat envelope. With η=δ/ωˉ≪1, writing z=ωˉt gives zcosz+sinz+O(η2)=0. Thus t∗​=2.028757838…/ωˉ+O(η2/ωˉ), using the first root of tanz=−z in (π/2,π). The envelope instead first reaches its maximum at π/(2δ).
